family: The single total certificate-prefix language in proof.md and family.py. At actual length N enumerate all prime2<=k<N, r=ceil((N-k)/k) with r>=3 and k>r+1, and all integer2<=t<r. Compute the exact d_t and B_t=t(t+3)/2 from proof.md Section1; require B_t<=d_t<N-k. Select the lexicographically least (4k+8d_t-4B_t-3,k,t). If none exists output0. Read the chosen k actual input bits as the lower coefficients of monic degree-k Q, reject invalid Q by the exact Frobenius/gcd test, and evaluate the descending-power BK elementary symmetric polynomial of order t on the remaining N-k bits with zero padding. Output its constant field coordinate. All prefix bits are counted in N; Q is input, not advice.
theorem: This fixed total language is in P, hence NP with empty witnesses. For every sufficiently large actual integer N, its admissible set is nonempty and C_B2(F_N)>=4N-L_N, where L_N is the complete minimum in the family definition. The supplied full-B2 finite theorem is4n-8d+min(5B-1,4B+3) under degree>=B on every d-dimensional affine space,1<=B<=d. Here every admissible payload has degree>=B_t>=5 on every d_t-space; the whole prefix language is not asserted to have that property. L_N/N^(4/5)->10*2^(1/5), so liminf C_B2(F_N)/N>=4 and the joint guarantee/projection is(4,1). For ANY admissible parameter sequence along actual lengths tending to infinity, liminf ell_N(k,t)/N^(4/5)>=10*2^(1/5), without assuming parameter-ratio convergence. This is optimality only of the supplied certificate, not actual circuits or other methods. Selected k/N^(3/5)->2^(2/5) and t/sqrt(r)->1. Against the fully specified two-prime adjacent-order reference F_dual in proof.md Section6, L_N<=L_dual-2 at every sufficiently large N. Infinitely many actual N_q=ceil((q^5/4)^(1/3)) have consecutive primes h=(8t_dual-20)(q-h)+2=Omega(N_q^(1/5)). No strict extra growing gain at every length or actual circuit-size ratio is claimed. The retained same-family coarse-threshold loss ratio tends to1/2 and the explicit two-stage reference complete-loss ratio is strictly below19/20, as proved in Section8.
